audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty prose is fine (EVEN, 5.5/10, 49.11% over 4394 games) but the level chart disagrees between layers: content win[] reads Orianna/Orianna/Skill/Viktor/Skill/Skill/Viktor (matching packet.levelChart) while every phases[N].side in the full layer reads 'Skill'. The page renders two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: packet.levelChart and content win[] agree with each other; the full layer is the outlier, so the full layer is what moves. Rows 3 and 6 also needed their why rewritten to match the Viktor verdict.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side -> Orianna, phases[1].side -> Orianna, phases[3].side -> Viktor (why rewritten to Hextech Ray clear), phases[6].side -> Viktor (why rewritten to range/Arcane Storm).

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes are keyed to Viktor 'augmenting E at 4-5', i.e. treated as a level timing.
audit.why: Glorious Evolution now buys augments with Hex Fragments earned on kills (100 per augment), not on level-ups. The upgrade timing is farm/kill dependent, so the advice 'freeze him off the upgrade timing at 4-5' is not grounded.
audit.corrected: Spike text now says augments come from Hex Fragments earned on kills, so denying kills delays them. Owner spikes kept: Lost Chapter, level 6 (R 110/95/80), Luden's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names ('Death Ray' for Hextech Ray (E), 'Chaos Storm' for Arcane Storm (R)), a fabricated effect ('silences'), and Gravity Field described as a root.
audit.why: The kit gives Hextech Ray (E, 12/11/10/9/8s, 525) and Arcane Storm (R, 120/100/80, 700) which interrupts channels — Riot's text says nothing about a silence. Gravity Field (W, 17/16/15/14/13s, 800) slows and stuns only enemies who stay in the field too long; it is not a root and it is dodgeable by stepping off.
audit.corrected: All names replaced with the kit names; 'silences' replaced with 'interrupts channels'; the stun described as dwell-based ('stuns only if you linger'). breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt around real numbers: Gravity Field 17s->13s, Hextech Ray 12s->8s, Orianna E 9s, R 110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere; breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all.
audit.why: Defect-catalogue item 3 — breakdown.cooldowns is the field that must hold real numbers.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Gravity Field 17s/13s, Hextech Ray 12s/8s, own E 9s and R 110s, plus what to do in each gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Siphon Power (Q) is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule 'autoreset-burst-tell': his combo opens with the Q empowered-auto, so the wind-up is the cue to step back.
audit.corrected: Folded into dosFull[2].d (his Q shield eats one hit) — the reset tell is the cue to disengage rather than trade the second auto.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[2].d all carried bodies belonging to other titles (the Gravity Field line and the tradeBad string).
audit.why: Defect-catalogue item 2 — title promises one thing, body explains another.
audit.corrected: Each body rewritten to match its own title.

edits.before: Late Ori is the teamfight: protect-ball on your diver, shockwave their clump, and dissonance the choke they retreat through.
edits.after: A finished Viktor out-ranges you: Arcane Storm chases while your ball has to travel 815 in. Shockwave picks, never duels.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Viktor wins by farming Hex Fragments off your deaths, augmenting Hextech Ray, and shoving you under tower every wave.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Command: Protect has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Viktor Gravity Field: 17s at rank 1, 13s at rank 5 — it stuns only if you linger, so step off it and his all-in has nothing. - Hextech Ray: 12s down to 8s — trade in that gap. - Your E is 9s and your R 110s at rank 1: E his commit, R only for a kill.

edits.before: Carry through the ball — no champion controls teamfight space like Orianna; one Shockwave on three is a won game, and you decide when it happens.
edits.after: Carry through the ball — Viktor pours his damage into a storm he has to steer, so a Shockwave that yanks him mid-fight costs him the whole zone.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Your ball sits where he must walk to last-hit, so Q-W lands the moment he steps up — 815 range means you never enter his 600.

edits.before: Viktor spends Gravity Field early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Your passive stacks on repeat autos — weave one after each Q; his Q shield eats one hit.

edits.before: That is Viktor’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Ball idle at 815 means no shield, no R — free Q trades for him.

edits.before: Poking with the ball stranded at max range when his engage is up — an Orianna without her ball is a Doran's Ring with legs.
edits.after: A 110-second ultimate spent on minions is a lost objective — hold R for the first clump that contests the river.

edits.before: Your range and ball beat him before his Death Ray is leveled - level 1 yours.
edits.after: Your ball harass beats him before Hextech Ray (E) is leveled - level 1 yours.

edits.before: His Death Ray comes online at 3 and the poke war levels off.
edits.after: His Hextech Ray comes online at 3 and the poke war levels off.

edits.before: Augmented Death Ray out-clears and out-pokes you through 4-5 - his favour.
edits.after: Augmented Hextech Ray out-clears and out-pokes you through 4-5 - his favour.

edits.before: Everything hinges on his augmented Death Ray (E). Before he upgrades it you win trades - land ball on him and pull back through him while his laser is still a single line. Once he augments E it splits and out-clears you, so this window flips to him; shove before that and freeze him off the upgrade timing.
edits.after: Everything hinges on his augmented Hextech Ray (E). Augments come from Hex Fragments he earns on kills, so denying kills delays it - before the upgrade you win trades: land ball on him and pull it back through him. Augmented, the ray adds an explosion behind it and out-clears you; shove first and freeze him off the farm.

edits.before: Both ults are up and the fight is even. His Chaos Storm (R) is a moving zone that silences and pokes; your Shockwave is burst engage. Neither of you gets a clean solo kill through the other's shield and E, so trade cooldowns rather than committing.
edits.after: Both ults are up and the fight is even. His Arcane Storm (R) is a redirectable zone that interrupts channels and chips; your Shockwave is a 110s burst engage. Neither of you kills through the other's shield and E, so trade cooldowns rather than committing.

edits.before: You spike together and it stays even - his Siphon Power (Q) shield-and-empowered-auto matches your poke while both of you build core. Don't step into his gravity field (W); a rooted Orianna eats his full combo.
edits.after: You spike together and it stays even - his Siphon Power (Q) shield-and-empowered-auto matches your poke while both of you build core. Gravity Field (W) stuns only if you linger - step off it and his combo has no lockdown.

edits.before: This is his half of the game. A completed Viktor with augmented E, W stun-zone and Chaos Storm out-DPSes and out-ranges you in extended fights. Play your Shockwave as a pick tool from max range, never a duel, and rely on your team to punish him while he channels R.
edits.after: This is his half of the game. A completed Viktor with augmented E, the Gravity Field stun-zone and Arcane Storm out-DPSes and out-ranges you in extended fights. Play Shockwave as a pick from your 815-range ball, never a duel, and collapse on him while he steers the storm.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours - your base range and ball harass beat him before his Death Ray is leveled, so step up and chunk him as he last-hits. He has no wave-clear edge yet, so shove and deny his early upgrade fragments.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours - your base range and ball harass beat him before Hextech Ray is leveled, so step up and chunk him as he last-hits. He has no wave-clear edge yet, so shove and deny his early Hex Fragments.

edits.before: Level 3 evens as his E comes online, and once he augments it at 4-5 the lane tilts to him - the split laser out-clears and out-pokes you, so you lose the shove war. At 6 both ults balance the fight; respect his gravity field and don't duel into his Chaos Storm.
edits.after: Level 3 evens as his E comes online, and once Hex Fragments augment it the lane tilts to him - the ray's explosion out-clears you, so you lose the shove war. At 6 both ults balance the fight; respect Gravity Field's dwell stun and don't duel into his Arcane Storm.

edits.before: Two-plus items is Viktor's kingdom - augmented E, W stun-zone and Chaos Storm out-range and out-DPS you in any sustained fight. Stop trying to win the sidelane and instead play Shockwave as a long-range pick, letting your team collapse while he is locked into his ult channel.
edits.after: Two-plus items is Viktor's kingdom - augmented E, the W stun-zone and Arcane Storm out-range and out-DPS you in any sustained fight. Stop trying to win the sidelane and play Shockwave as a long-range pick, letting your team collapse on him while he steers the storm.

notes: suspectNames flagged wants.you[2] 'Land Shockwave' — false positive, Shockwave is the correct short form of Command: Shockwave; left alone. phases[N].rating left untouched: the polarity of that number (owner-favour vs difficulty) is not derivable from the data, and guessing would have flipped six rows the wrong way — see questionsForUser. breakdown.wave is Orianna-generic (no Viktor content) but a grounded rewrite did not fit the length band without dropping real wave advice; left as-is. Riot's R text says Arcane Storm interrupts enemy channels; the kit's derived 'channel: interruptible' flag on the same ability is unverified for Viktor's own cast, so no claim was made that CC cancels his R.
